summary.short: Interim final rule amending the Export Administration Regulations to license exports, reexports and in-country transfers of advanced computing chips, related computers and semiconductor manufacturing equipment to China; adds supercomputer and chip-fab end-use controls, Entity List foreign-direct-product rules and a temporary supply-chain general license, effective 7–21 October 2022.
summary.long: Interim final rule of the Bureau of Industry and Security amending the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Adds ECCNs 3A090, 4A090 and related software and technology, and 3B090 for certain semiconductor manufacturing equipment, to the Commerce Control List with regional stability (RS) license requirements for exports, reexports and in-country transfers to China, subject to a presumption of denial. Adds Advanced computing and Supercomputer foreign direct product rules (§ 734.9(h), (i)) and a footnote 4 Entity List FDP rule. Adds § 744.23 end-use prohibitions for supercomputers and certain PRC chip fabrication facilities, with no license exceptions and a BIS 'is informed' mechanism. Amends § 744.6 to inform U.S. persons that certain support activities require a license. Expands license requirements for 28 Entity List entities in China. Creates a temporary general license for supply-chain activities from 21 October 2022 to 7 April 2023 and a model certification in supplement no. 1 to part 734. Most provisions take effect 7, 12 or 21 October 2022; comments were due 12 December 2022.

enforcement.note: The text sets license requirements, presumptions of denial and end-use prohibitions, but states no penalty, fine, criminal sanction, license revocation, clawback, suspension or blocking. It cites ECRA (50 U.S.C. 4801-4852) only as legal basis. The one penalty reference, in the Paperwork Reduction Act paragraph, limits penalties for uncontrolled information collections and is not a sanction regime.
